text:
maya: heads up — after the 2.1 runtime rollout i'm seeing a clear p99 host-side decode latency bump for short prompts (<50 tokens). traces point at host parsing/tokenization + more KV-cache churn during streaming. flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/local/27142/fg.svg

igor: can you repro locally? example request + exact timing would help.

maya: repro steps: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rw-medium","prompt":"short prompt","max_tokens":20,"stream":true}' --progress-bar
observed: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 110ms, p99 ~ 270-320ms (host decode portion). single-run flame: host_parse 18%, tokenization 12%, grpc_writev 9%, runtime_decode 20%, user 30%.

ravi: fwiw our kvcache metrics show evictions spike aligned with streaming chunk boundaries -- when frame payload < 256 bytes we get repeated small writes and kv access churn. maybe the new framing/parse path is breaking our coalescing.

deploy-bot: rollout/2.1 completed by ci-pipeline at 2026-03-10T03:12:05Z :white_check_mark:

sam: could be two things: (1) kernel selection now favors a generic attention kernel for short seqs (slower) and (2) host framing changed so we lose writev coalescing. both would hit short prompts the hardest.

leo: i ran a quick perf microbench on the canary host. flame samples attached: small-req (16 tokens): host_parse ~ 22%, grpc overhead ~ 11%, kvcache lookup ~ 14%. larger-req (256 tokens) shows much lower host_parse%.

igor: any recent changes to batching heuristics? we had a tweak that reduced the batching window to favor latency. that could shrink batch formation and increase per-request overhead.

maya: yes the batching window was changed in 2.1: default timer went from 6ms -> 2ms for low-latency tier. that helped medium+ requests but for tiny prompts it starves batching and increases number of small frames.

ravi: small frames + early kvcache eviction = thrash. hypothesis: parser now creates sub-frames for streaming tokens that end up evicting kvcache entries before the request finishes. also we do utf8 validation per-fragment which is expensive.

sam: actionable experiments i propose:
- revert batching window to 6ms on canary (A/B)
- re-enable writev coalescing in host-proxy for small-stream payloads
- add ascii-fastpath: skip utf8 validation for typical ascii-only prompts behind a feature flag
- force attention-kernel pin for short seqs to test perf delta
run microbench with kvcache and parse counters.

leo: i can run the kernel pin experiment. quick results: forcing optimized short-kernel drops decode p99 from ~300ms -> ~160ms in microbench (host portion reduced ~90ms).

igor: that suggests kernel selection is definitely part of it. but the kvcache and parse overhead still account for ~100ms. need combined approach.

maya: quick patch idea for parse: in ingress framers/streaming_parser.cc add "if (likely_ascii(buf)) skip_utf8_check();" — low risk behind flag, big payoff for english-only prompts. also aggregate small frames into a single processing buffer before tokenization.

ravi: careful — aggregator increases tail latency for some burst patterns. recommend adaptive aggregator: coalesce until either size >= 512 or elapsed >= 3ms. pseudocode:
```
start = now(); buffer = [];
while(now()-start < max_wait && buffer.size < max_bytes) read_frame_append();
process(buffer);
```
set max_wait by tier (canary: 3ms).

sam: i'll schedule canary runs: revert batch timer (6ms) + enable aggregator(3ms) + ascii-fastpath. we'll collect kvcache.evictions, parse.cpu_ms, grpc.writev_count, and p99 decode.

leo: where do we put dashboards? i've added a small dashboard: /dashboards/eng-runtime/parse-kv-grpc-27142 (shared).

maya: quick numbers from a local run with aggregator+ascii-fastpath+kernel-pin: p50 40ms, p95 85ms, p99 140ms — still above pre-2.1 p99 (~110ms) but much better. kvcache evictions down 3x, grpc.writev_count down 60%.

igor: good. next steps:
- sam: run canary A/B for 6 hours collecting traces & kvcache metrics (owner: sam)
- leo: kernel-pin smoke in dedicated infra (owner: leo)
- maya: prepare parse-aggregator/fastpath patch PR behind feature flags + perf unit tests (owner: maya)
- ravi: add kvcache metrics export for small-fragment events and set alert if evictions spike > 2x baseline (owner: ravi)

maya: creating a short 30min triage today 14:30 PT to align on rollout plan and rollback thresholds. i'll post calendar invite. :calendar:

sam: noted, will run the first canary batch right after triage. :thumbsup:

ravi: adding a log line to streaming parser to help correlate fragment sizes to kvcache events (low overhead) — will turn on for canary only.

maya: thanks all. i'll open the PRs and link here. we'll iterate quickly if canary shows regressions. :rocket:
